Tell me in about 200 words why people in India are switching to UPI, with a short list of 3 reasons
7:15 PM

UPI has become India's default way to pay because it is free, fast and works almost everywhere. You scan a code or type a number, enter your PIN, and the money moves between bank accounts in seconds. No cash to carry, no change to hunt for, no card machine needed.

For shopkeepers it is just as easy. A printed QR code costs next to nothing, so even a tea stall or a vegetable cart can accept digital payments. That is why you now see UPI in small towns and villages, not only in big cities. Friends and family also use it to split bills and send money at any hour, including holidays.

Another push came from apps like PhonePe, Google Pay and Paytm, which made it simple to use, and from the government, which backed it as a public system. As more people used it, more shops accepted it, and that pulled in still more users.

Here are three reasons in short:

Free and instant: Most everyday payments cost nothing and arrive in seconds.
Easy for everyone: A phone and a bank account are enough, for buyers and sellers alike.
Accepted everywhere: From malls to street stalls, one QR code works across apps.

Numbers and rules can change, so treat this as a general picture rather than fresh figures.

What is a good name for a pet tortoise?
7:15 PM

Shelly is my top pick, simple and a little cheeky. A few more:

Turbo: funny because tortoises are the opposite of fast.
Biscuit: small, round and sweet.
Gulab: after the jamun, slow and delightful.
